title: Discovery of the Proton — Anode Rays and Nuclear Transmutation
topicTitle: Discovery Of Proton And Its Properties
notes: How the proton was found: Goldstein's anode (canal) rays, the mass spectrometry evidence, and Rutherford's 1919 transmutation — the second particle needed to build the nuclear atom.

Goldstein used a perforated (perforated-cathode) discharge tube: besides cathode rays, a new radiation passed *through* the holes of the cathode in the direction opposite to cathode rays. Properties: travel in straight lines, deflected by E and B fields in the direction of *positive* charges, and the e/m value **depends on the gas** in the tube — so these are positive ions of the gas, not a universal particle.

With hydrogen in the tube the e/m is the largest observed (9.58 × 10⁷ C kg⁻¹), i.e. the lightest positive particle: the proton, with charge +1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 1.00728 u ≈ 1836 electron masses. The proton is the nuclear constituent that carries the atomic number Z.

Bombarding nitrogen with α-particles produced protons and oxygen: $^{14}\text{N}+\,^{4}\text{He}\rightarrow\,^{17}\text{O}+\,^{1}\text{p}$. This was the first artificial nuclear reaction: it (i) proved protons exist inside nuclei, (ii) changed one element into another (contra Dalton), and (iii) named the particle 'proton' (from protos, first).
### Why the proton matters for structure

The nuclear charge Z counted in protons is the element's identity (Moseley); A = Z + N requires neutrons as well, since protons alone cannot account for the masses and stability of nuclei (electrostatic repulsion of like charges would fly apart — the strong interaction and neutrons are needed).
confusion: ❌ Anode rays are a universal particle like cathode rays. ✅ Their e/m depends on the gas — they are positive ions of that gas; only the hydrogen ion (proton) is universal.
❌ Goldstein named and identified the proton fully. ✅ He discovered the rays; the proton was characterised later and named by Rutherford.
❌ The proton is 1837 times heavier than the electron. ✅ 1836 (the neutron is 1839).

universalFacts: The proton's mass in u is 1.00728 — the basis of the amu scale (¹²C = 12 exactly).
Canal rays are also called positive rays; Aston's mass spectrograph (1919) developed from them.
Rutherford's transmutation opened nuclear chemistry: element synthesis beyond bismuth became possible.
examples: **Problem:** Why do anode rays bend less than cathode rays in the same field? **Solution:** deflection ∝ q/m; the proton's q/m is ≈1836 times smaller than the electron's, so its curvature is correspondingly tiny.
